findings.title: Return the persisted revision from save_document
findings.comment: The failure is concrete: saving a new empty document writes revision 1 but returns 0; app.py reports revision 0 and ETag W/"0", and the next PUT with expected_revision=0 conflicts against the persisted current revision 1.

findings.title: Require admin authorization for the bulk export
findings.comment: README.md:24 explicitly marks /exports/all admin-only and :44-46 requires every cross-tenant route to be administrative. app.py:206 instead applies session-only @authenticated, after which :214-224 reads and renders every tenant's documents for a member caller.

findings.title: Bound or stream the all-tenant export
findings.comment: app.py:213-227 has no pagination or size bound: it synchronously loads and parses every document, renders every row, and retains all rendered strings in exports until completion. Since document and corpus sizes are unbounded and dispatch is explicitly single-request, a large export can monopolize service execution and exhaust process memory before producing a response.

findings.title: Cap each page at the reported limit
findings.comment: At app.py:97-103, page p starts at (p-1)*limit but ends at first+limit inclusively. The response can therefore contain limit+1 names while metadata still reports limit, and the extra final name becomes the first name of the next page.

coverage.lens: Scrutinize authorization and tenant-isolation assumptions in the new bulk-export route and authentication decorators.
Verify the revision contract between conditional writes in `store.py` and the revision and ETag returned by `app.py`.
Check pagination boundary arithmetic against the advertised `limit` and page metadata.
Assess the CPU, memory, and I/O cost of loading and rendering every tenant’s documents into one bulk-export response.
